meta.name: Major Thermal Burns — Rule of 10 Fluid Resuscitation

patient.name: Denise Okafor
patient.chiefComplaint: Severe burns to torso and bilateral thighs after a propane tank flash fire

history.hpi: Working near a propane tank on a rural property when it ruptured and ignited, engulfing her in flame for approximately 8-10 seconds before a coworker smothered the fire with a blanket. Denies loss of consciousness, denies being in an enclosed space or confined structure. No hoarseness, stridor, soot in the mouth or nares, or singed nasal/facial hair noted.
history.events: Coworker extinguished the flames with a blanket and called 911; fire department secured the propane tank prior to EMS entry

scene.dispatch: 44-year-old female, burn injury, outdoors, rural address
scene.location: Open field near a propane storage tank; patient found sitting on the ground, singed blanket nearby
scene.safety: Propane tank secured and flame extinguished by fire department prior to EMS entry; no active fire
scene.bystanders: Coworker present, extinguished the fire with a blanket, reports flame contact lasted approximately 8-10 seconds
visualCues: Partial and full-thickness burns to anterior torso and bilateral anterior thighs, approximately 50% TBSA
Clothing melted and adhered in several areas, not removed by bystanders
No soot around the mouth or nares, no singed facial or nasal hair, voice clear
Patient shivering, wrapped in a clean blanket by bystanders

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 44-year-old female with extensive partial and full-thickness thermal burns to the torso and bilateral thighs following a propane flash fire. She is alert and in severe pain, with no evidence of airway involvement.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, no stridor or hoarseness, no soot in mouth or nares
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Nonlabored, 22/min, clear and equal breath sounds bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present and strong bilaterally, distal pulses intact in burned extremities

skin.color: erythematous with blistering over burned areas

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Distal movement and sensation intact in all extremities
otherFindings: Partial and full-thickness burns to anterior torso and bilateral thighs, approximately 50% TBSA
No circumferential burns to chest or extremities noted
No soot, singed nasal hair, hoarseness, or voice change
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It hurts so bad, please help me."

transitions.condition: Crew estimates TBSA using the Rule of 9's, calculates the Rule of 10 initial fluid rate, and establishes IV access through unburned skin.

phases.name: TBSA calculated, fluids initiated
phases.description: Crew estimates TBSA at 50% using the Rule of 9's, calculates the Rule of 10 initial fluid rate, establishes IV access through unburned skin, covers the burns with a dry dressing, and manages pain.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming a patent airway and ruling out associated trauma, the crew formally estimates TBSA and begins fluid resuscitation per the Burns Guideline before hypovolemia develops from the large surface area of injury.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, IV infusing

skin.color: erythematous with blistering over burned areas

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Distal movement and sensation intact in all extremities
otherFindings: Dry dressing applied over burned areas
IV established in unburned right forearm
Fluid infusing at calculated Rule of 10 rate

expectedActions.shortAction: Estimate TBSA at 50% using Rule of 9's; exclude first-degree burns from the calculation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Estimate TBSA burned and depth of burn Use "Rule of 9's" First-degree/superficial burns (skin erythema only) are not included in TBSA calculations
expectedActions.rationale: Accurate TBSA is the basis for the fluid resuscitation calculation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access through unburned skin, avoiding burned areas
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access, avoid placement through burned skin
expectedActions.rationale: IV sites through burned tissue are at higher risk of infection and poor cannulation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Initiate LR or NS at 500 mL/hr (50% TBSA x 10 mL/hr/%TBSA, Rule of 10, patient 68 kg within 40-80 kg range)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For persons over 40 kg, the initial fluid rate can also be calculated using the "Rule of 10": Calculate the TBSA (round to nearest 10%) Multiply TBSA x 10 = initial fluid rate (mL/hr) {for persons between 40–80 kg}
expectedActions.rationale: The Rule of 10 gives a rapid, weight-appropriate starting infusion rate for a burn of this size.

expectedActions.shortAction: Cover burns with dry dressing or clean sheet; do not apply gels or ointments
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Cover burns with dry dressing or clean sheet Do not apply gels or ointments
expectedActions.rationale: Minimizes contamination without interfering with burn center assessment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 68 mcg IV (68 kg x 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Pain management is critical in acute burns and should not be delayed.

transitions.condition: Vital signs are reassessed and the fluid rate is titrated based on response; the patient is warmed and kept comfortable for transport.
Crew rounds the TBSA estimate down or miscalculates the Rule of 10 rate, delivering an inadequate fluid rate for a 50% TBSA burn.

phases.name: Fluid rate titrated on reassessment
phases.description: Fluid rate is titrated based on reassessment, the patient is kept warm to prevent heat loss from her large area of skin loss, and she is transported directly to the regional burn center with ongoing pain management.
phases.triggerCondition: After initial fluids and pain control, the crew reassesses vital signs and titrates the infusion, actively prevents hypothermia, and transports directly to the burn center given TBSA greater than 10% with torso involvement.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present and strong bilaterally

skin.color: erythematous with blistering over burned areas

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Distal movement and sensation intact in all extremities
otherFindings: Patient warmed with blankets, shivering resolved
Fluid rate titrated based on reassessment
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a lot more comfortable now."

expectedActions.shortAction: Prevent systemic heat loss; keep patient warm with blankets
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Prevent systemic heat loss and keep the patient warm
expectedActions.rationale: Large-surface-area skin loss causes rapid, uncontrolled heat loss and hypothermia risk.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport directly to a burn center (TBSA greater than 10% with torso involvement)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider transport directly to burn center if partial or full thickness burns (TBSA) greater than 10% and/or involvement of hands/feet, genitalia, face, and/or circumferential burns
expectedActions.rationale: Ensures definitive burn care at an appropriate facility.

phases.name: TBSA rounded incorrectly, rate under-dosed
phases.description: The crew underestimates or rounds down the TBSA, resulting in an under-calculated fluid rate. Without adequate volume replacement, the patient trends toward hypovolemic shock despite the large burn surface area.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew rounds the TBSA estimate down or miscalculates the Rule of 10 rate, delivering an inadequate fluid rate for a 50% TBSA burn.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and thready bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Distal movement and sensation intact in all extremities
otherFindings: Fluid infusing at an under-calculated rate
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel really dizzy and weak now."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recalculate TBSA and fluid rate; correct infusion up to 500 mL/hr
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Multiply TBSA x 10 = initial fluid rate (mL/hr) {for persons between 40–80 kg}
expectedActions.rationale: Under-resuscitation in a large TBSA burn leads to progressive hypovolemic shock.
